newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia watchdog backs foreign media owners.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia watchdog backs foreign media owners.

text.p: Australia's trade practices watchdog, the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC), on Tuesday called for looser restrictions on foreign investment in media businesses.

The commission had said as much in its submission to the government's review of the other main area of media regulation, the cross-ownership limits on investors holding stakes in different types of media, ACCC chairman Allan Fels said.

"We, in our submission, suggest that the present (foreign ownership) restrictions are much too restrictive but we don't say that that shouldn't be a factor that's looked at in the media ownership debate," he said in a radio interview.
"But there may be some trade-offs. We may need a more flexible approach than rigid rules about the degree of foreign ownership such as we have at the present time."
Fells said that relaxation of the cross-media ownership limits without a loosening of foreign ownership would tend to concentrate the number of players.

"I do think that there are some reasons why one would treat media as being different from other parts of industry, and that is that we are interested not only in there being competition but also in there being a degree of diversity and plurality about the media."

"If you think the media is special on that account then it does mean not only that you might have some special cross media laws but you want to make sure the foreign ownership laws don't cut across that objective."
The government is reviewing media ownership laws, but has said its review does not cover foreign ownership.
Canadian media baron Conrad Black has said he would consider selling out of newspaper publisher John Fairfax Holdings Ltd if he cannot lift his present 25 percent stake to 50 percent.
Australia's media rules prevent foreigners from holding more than 25 percent of a newspaper group and more than 15 percent of a television company.
Communications Minister Richard Alston last week ruled out widening the government's media industry review to include foreign ownership.
